episodes.title: The Stolen Bride
episodes.blurb: On the night of his wedding in Kiev, Prince Ruslan sees his bride Ludmila vanish in thunder and smoke. Cantos I to III: the three rival suitors, the sorcerer Finn and his sad love story, the magic garden of the wizard Chernomor, the cap that makes a girl invisible, and a gigantic talking head guarding a sword.

episodes.title: The Beard and the Living Water
episodes.blurb: Cantos IV to VI: the castle of the twelve maidens, Ludmila hiding invisible in the wizard's garden, the flight over the sea clinging to a magic beard, a faithless friend, and the living and dead water that bring a dead hero back to save Kiev.

glossary: Prince Vladimir
“Vladimir the Red Sun”, the Grand Prince of Kiev (reigned about 980–1015), the generous ruler of the Russian epic songs; here he is Ludmila's father.
Kiev and the Dnieper
the old capital of Rus on the Dnieper river, in today's Ukraine.
Bayan
a legendary bard of ancient Rus who sings to the gusli, a plucked harp-like instrument.
Lel
the Slavic god of love, as Pushkin names him.
Chernomor
the dwarf wizard of the northern mountains, whose power lies in his long beard.
Finn
a sorcerer from the far north. Finland was thought of as the home of the best magicians.
Pechenegs
a nomad people of the steppe who raided Kiev in the 10th and 11th centuries.
Khazars
a Turkic people of the steppe north of the Caucasus; Ratmir is a khan of theirs.
Baba Yaga and Koshchei
the witch in a flying mortar and the deathless miser king of Russian fairy tales.
mead
a drink of fermented honey, served at feasts in the old halls.
sarafan
a long sleeveless Russian dress worn over a blouse.
Moors
the dark-skinned servants and guards of the palace, as the original calls them.
Orlovsky
Alexander Orlovsky, a Russian painter famous for lively battle and horse scenes.
the northern Orpheus
Vasily Zhukovsky, Pushkin's older fellow poet, whose ballad about twelve sleeping maidens Pushkin gently mocks.
Armida
the enchantress whose magic gardens are famous in Tasso's epic.
summary: On his wedding night the young prince Ruslan loses his bride Ludmila to an evil wizard and rides out to find her, through enchanted forests, a talking giant head, rival knights and a magic beard. Pushkin's first great poem, a fairy tale told with wit.
site_description: At the wedding feast of the Kiev prince's daughter Ludmila a clap of thunder puts out the lights, and the bride is gone, carried off by the dwarf wizard Chernomor. Three rivals and the bridegroom Ruslan ride out to find her. Pushkin's first great poem (1820), full of fairy-tale wonders, jokes and tender asides, here read as a full-cast English audiobook in a prose rendering of the Russian verse.
text_note: Prose rendering of the Russian verse by an AI, a draft that needs a human editor.

ru.description: На свадебном пиру в Киеве гремит гром, гаснет свет, и Людмила исчезает: её похитил злой карлик Черномор. Руслан и три его соперника скачут на поиски. Первая поэма Пушкина (1820), сказка с шуткой и лирическими отступлениями.
